text: Lesson 14 required mapping handlers to be deterministic. The EVM has the identical requirement. An HTTP call might return different answers at the same moment, which is exactly why a smart contract cannot make one.
Most of what makes smart contracts useful depends on external data. None of it originates on-chain, and none of it can be fetched by the contract itself. Something has to get it there: an oracle.
The simplest oracle is one trusted server pushing a value on-chain. That's a single point of failure and trust — it hasn't removed a trusted intermediary, just renamed it.

A real fix needs what blockchain consensus itself relies on: multiple independent nodes retrieving data independently, aggregating their answers, with real economic cost for lying or failing to deliver.
That's the oracle problem, and it's specifically what Chainlink exists to solve. Next up: Chainlink's price feeds, the most widely used oracle in production today.
